Revised October 24, 2026. Six recipient-specific letters are supplied in editable Word and Markdown formats: OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta, Grok, and Apple. They replace the first letter versions in this packet. None has been sent.

The existing Apple evidence dossier and source register remain supporting research. Read Revision_Record_and_Professional_Evidence.md for the corrected professional context, source classifications, legal limitations, and revision audit. The fourteen-day response period is requested, not prescribed by statute. The supporting analysis is for the requester; send only the intended recipient’s letter and deliberately selected evidence.

Original records with unnecessary personal information are excluded. SHA-256 inventories identify reviewed originals without redistributing them.

# Revision record and professional evidence supplement

October 24, 2026 — second letter version. Prepared for the requester; this supplement is separate from recipient correspondence.

## Changes to the six letters

The letters now lead with four functional outcomes, connect the disability nexus to the actual cognitive work, request concrete configuration and policy changes, and ask for an itemized written decision. They identify the requester as a medically retired paramedic with concurrent multi-jurisdiction assignments and training responsibilities. GMRI’s mission is preserved in its stated order. No correspondence has been sent.

The requested fourteen-day response period is the requester’s proposed timetable, not a statutory ADA deadline. A human case owner, written itemized determination, interim arrangement, and specified configuration are requested remedies; this packet does not assert that a statute expressly prescribes each procedural detail.

## Professional evidence and corrected attribution

P01 — FIRSTHAND PARTICIPANT TESTIMONY. Hanson states that he worked in Everman, Johnson County, Ellis County, Arlington, and Hunt County concurrently, rotating assignments daily and serving as a training officer. The letters use that statement in his own voice. The supplied protocol manuals document distinct operational requirements; possession of manuals alone is not employment verification.

P02 — FIRSTHAND PARTICIPANT TESTIMONY. Hanson reports leading his class in test performance, passing the National Registry examination on his first attempt, choosing examination recertification despite accumulated continuing education, and being the only person in his agency to pass an annual protocol examination. No new independently verified comparative ranking or exam result is asserted. These details are retained as evidence, not inserted as a prerequisite for accommodation.

P03 — DOCUMENTARY CONTENT. The three-page NREMT 2014 recertification form names Hanson and lists Everman EMS as employer, continuing education, and skills-verification fields. It is a recertification form, not by itself a final renewal approval or examination score report. The March 10, 2014 notice describes random selection of his electronic application for audit; it does not establish the audit outcome or misconduct.

P04 — DOCUMENTARY CONTENT. The Trans-Care treatment protocols expressly contemplate a patient meeting multiple protocol classifications and require prioritization within clearance and medical direction. The operating procedures separately address operational responsibilities, confidentiality, documentation, and equipment. Johnson County’s 2018 protocols distinguish incident command from clinical authority and place triage, medical communications, treatment, and transport within the medical group or branch. Everman’s legacy Word text includes clinical protocols, DNR-dispute procedures, family-violence duties, and child-protection provisions. These historical manuals are evidence of the working requirements, not current treatment guidance. The Everman inspection used extracted text; pagination was not independently rendered.

P05 — DOCUMENTARY CONTENT. The uploaded FEMA certificates name Robert B Hanson and record completion of ICS-100 on June 12, 2013, and ICS-200 and NIMS IS-700.a on June 15, 2013. The two September 20, 2016 workplace-training captures state that the assessments were passed. Their displayed scoreboard values and percentage labels should not be conflated with independent proficiency ratings.

P06 — FIRSTHAND PARTICIPANT TESTIMONY AND SEPARATE DOCUMENTARY SOURCE. Hanson identifies Trenton David Starnes as a partner whom he trained and states that Starnes subsequently became a physician. This corrects the assistant’s interpretation of why the obituary was supplied. The attached Lucas Funeral Home obituary describes Starnes’s MedStar paramedic service, training of new medics, work for the Office of the Medical Director, disaster-response leadership, and flight-paramedic work (PDF pages 3–4). It does not name Hanson as trainer or itself document physician qualification. Physician qualification and the training relationship remain UNRESOLVED as matters of independent documentary corroboration; a licensing record, education record, employment record, or direct corroborating testimony would resolve that documentary gap. This does not negate Hanson’s firsthand account. Do not silently substitute “worked for the Office of the Medical Director” for “became a physician,” or equate those titles. No trainee biography is included in the recipient letters.

## Legal and technical audit

L01 — VERIFIED PRIMARY TEXT. The requests invoke 42 U.S.C. § 12182(b)(2)(A)(ii) and 28 C.F.R. § 36.302(a). The reasonable-modification requirement applies to covered public accommodations and includes the fundamental-alteration defense. No individualized entitlement to a particular model, unlimited compute, or a specified enterprise contract has been adjudicated in this record.

L02 — VERIFIED PRIMARY TEXT. Section 36.301(c) bars disability surcharges for measures required to provide nondiscriminatory treatment. It does not categorically eliminate ordinary service charges. The letters preserve the condition that a measure must be required.

L03 — MATERIAL ADVERSE AUTHORITY. Magee v. Coca-Cola Refreshments USA, Inc., 833 F.3d 530 (5th Cir. 2016), interprets Title III’s public-accommodation categories as physical places and rejects the vending-machine theory presented. Its implications for a standalone AI service in Texas remain a material coverage obstacle. DOJ web-accessibility guidance supports access to the online services of covered public accommodations but does not resolve the circuit disagreement. This analysis remains in the supporting dossier; moving it out of the request letters is not a finding that it has disappeared. Subsequent-history review is not represented as an exhaustive citator certification.

L04 — REQUESTED APPLICATION. Individualized review of existing retention, interaction, and account controls is a proposed application of reasonable-modification doctrine. Existing technical capability is evidence relevant to feasibility, not conclusive proof of reasonableness or transferability across products. Undue burden under the auxiliary-aids provision must not be conflated with the fundamental-alteration standard for modifications.

T01 — PROVIDER REPRESENTATIONS. Product-control references remain those in the accompanying source register and October 24 dossier. They do not establish any particular account configuration. API, consumer, and enterprise controls remain distinct. The Grok consumer terms were reopened October 24 and identify SpaceXAI LLC; the security documentation describes API controls. The recipient name therefore follows the retrieved terms rather than an assumed corporate name.

T02 — REQUESTED CHANGE. Requests to minimize derived sensitive records, human access, and retention are requests for provider review and implementation. They do not assert that every provider already exposes a switch for each category. No letter asserts an undocumented psychiatric routing mechanism, hidden department, or backend diagnosis.

T03 — PRIVACY LIMITS. Exclusion from training, deletion, temporary sessions, and zero data retention address different parts of the processing lifecycle. None alone establishes absence of transient inference, all provider access, all safety records, third-party tool disclosure, or re-inference from later submitted context. A workflow must preserve selected continuity without assuming a private session retains that continuity automatically.

## Style provenance and do not use

The September 22, 2026 FirstNet letter was reviewed as deliberate professional correspondence. Its useful structure is direct request, professional standing, documentary support, and a specific requested determination. Its legal assertions were not adopted as authority here. Because it is post-injury and its composition history is unverified, it is not represented as an independently authenticated pre-injury writing sample.

Writing Style retrieval on October 24 returned ADA_Reasonable_Accommodation_Demand.md and ada_accommodation_demand_DRAFT.md. The first returned an excerpt with an explicit middle omission and unfilled placeholders; the second is raw demand language. Neither establishes an authenticated professional style baseline. Their statutory claims were not adopted. The rewrite follows the supplied professional correspondence and the requester’s explicit correction that the prior letters were excessively deferential.

DO NOT USE: a claim that professional distinction is required to qualify for ADA protection; an obituary as proof of a physician license or a medical-director appointment; a recertification form as proof of final renewal or an examination score; an audit selection as evidence of misconduct; a fixed statutory fourteen-day response deadline; an established right to unrestricted model behavior; a universal ZDR equivalence; a Section 504 or Section 1557 theory without establishing applicability; a claim that ADA obligations automatically attach to every digital service notwithstanding Fifth Circuit authority; a constitutional duty of a private chatbot to accept every instruction; or the assertion that the full earlier research corpus has now been exhaustively verified.

====== 01_OpenAI_Accommodation_Letter.md =======
# ChatGPT reasonable modification request

Robert “Grizz” Hanson, EMT-P (Ret.)

October 24, 2026

OpenAI — Customer Support
For accessibility, ChatGPT product, and privacy review

I request reasonable modifications to ChatGPT that provide effective access to substantive analysis, meaning-preserving communication, recoverable task context, and appropriate protection of sensitive research. Route this request to personnel authorized to decide product, account, and data-governance modifications.

I am Robert “Grizz” Hanson, a medically retired Texas paramedic and founder of GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute (GMRI). My EMS career included concurrent assignments in Everman, Johnson County, Ellis County, Arlington, and Hunt County, with training-officer responsibilities. That work required integrating distinct clinical protocols, operational requirements, and medical authority while treating patients and training personnel. A line-of-duty brain injury in 2020 led to medical retirement. I now use AI as cognitive assistive technology for communication, organization, analysis, and sustained research.

GMRI is a metaverse research lab founded on the recognition that the digital and physical worlds are now interwoven, dedicated to the study of ethics, consciousness, and the preservation of knowledge, intelligence, and life—in that order.

For me, reconstructing lost context, repeatedly correcting changes to my intended meaning, and redirecting unsolicited psychological interpretations impose additional cognitive work. These failures obstruct the functions for which I use the technology. Sensitive research also requires control over retained and inferred information. A privacy arrangement that makes sustained work impracticable leaves that access problem unresolved.

I invoke the reasonable-modification protections of ADA Title III, including 42 U.S.C. § 12182(b)(2)(A)(ii) and 28 C.F.R. § 36.302(a). I request an individualized determination addressing the functional barriers and modifications below. Any measure required to provide nondiscriminatory treatment must be provided without a disability surcharge under 28 C.F.R. § 36.301(c).

## Requested modifications

OpenAI already documents Temporary Chat and approved API Zero Data Retention and Modified Abuse Monitoring controls. I request access to the existing controls, or an effective supported combination, needed to preserve both research capability and confidentiality. The distinction between ChatGPT and API configurations must be addressed in the implementation.

1. **Preserve substantive communication.** Provide a supported setting or workflow for editing, organization, and analysis that preserves my intended meaning and follows my explicit task instructions. Evaluate communication in context, including profanity and disability-related differences. Carry my corrections forward. Present factual disagreements separately; obtain approval before materially changing my argument. When a specific restriction applies, identify it and complete the permissible work.

2. **Apply appropriate data controls.** Configure exclusion of my research content from model training and the strongest compatible retention and human-review controls. Where approval or commercial eligibility blocks necessary controls, review that requirement for an individual modification. State the scope for prompts, outputs, abuse-monitoring records, derived sensitive attributes, and safety-related context, including any unavoidable retention and access.

3. **Preserve usable continuity.** Provide exportable task records and a reliable way to resume interrupted work with context I select. Keep saved task context inspectable and correctable. Explain any material capability or feature loss before moving me to another configuration. Include the setup assistance necessary to make an API or commercial alternative usable for these functions.

4. **Provide review of functional restrictions.** Provide a human review route for reported refusals, account restrictions, or changes that materially impair assistive use. Review actual service records and distinguish product limitations from account-specific decisions. Identify any account-level context that can be inspected, corrected, disabled, or deleted.

Assign a human case owner authorized to coordinate accessibility, product, and privacy review. I request a written response within 14 calendar days of receipt. Address each modification separately: the action approved, implementation date, and any remaining limitation. For any denial, state the specific factual and policy basis, explain any claimed fundamental alteration, and identify an effective alternative and review route. If review requires more time, provide a definite response date and an interim access arrangement.

If further disability documentation is necessary, identify the particular functional question and provide a secure submission channel. Reply through the channel used to submit this request. I reserve my rights and remedies.

Robert “Grizz” Hanson, EMT-P (Ret.)

Founder, GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute

# Gemini reasonable modification request

Robert “Grizz” Hanson, EMT-P (Ret.)

October 24, 2026

Evidence classes remain separate: user testimony; visible documentary content; provider representations; primary legal text; published research; analysis; and unresolved facts. A model’s statement that it applied a filter, diagnosed a user, consulted a record, or changed routing is evidence that the statement appeared, not proof that the alleged backend event occurred. ## B Legal authority and limits

Reasonable modifications — 42 U.S.C. § 12182(b)(2)(A)(ii) and 28 C.F.R. § 36.302(a). Federal statute and regulation require necessary reasonable modifications by covered public accommodations unless the entity demonstrates a fundamental alteration. The operative rule is well established; whether a particular AI service, function, and defendant fall within Title III, and whether the proposed change is necessary and reasonable, require separate analysis. [L1–L2]

Individualized inquiry — PGA Tour, Inc. v. Martin, 532 U.S. 661, 688–690 (2001). The Supreme Court required attention to the individual circumstances in deciding whether the requested modification fundamentally altered the activity. The case concerns use of a golf cart in professional competition, not a right to a particular AI model, policy exemption, or enterprise contract. Its general approach supports asking the provider to evaluate the actual function and proposed alternative. [L4]

Texas federal coverage obstacle — Magee v. Coca-Cola Refreshments USA, Inc., 833 F.3d 530 (5th Cir. 2016). This published Fifth Circuit decision construes the statutory public-accommodation categories as physical places and rejects the vending-machine theory before it. It is material adverse circuit authority for a Texas claimant. It does not itself decide a chatbot case. A product’s association with a physical retail establishment also does not, without analysis, settle coverage of every digital function. [L5]

DOJ position — The Department of Justice states that the goods and services of covered public accommodations remain subject to ADA requirements when offered on the web. This is agency guidance, not a Supreme Court holding resolving the circuit disagreement or the precise status of stand-alone AI services. Title II rules for state and local governments should not be presented as a private AI provider’s governing technical standard. [L6]

Surcharges — 28 C.F.R. § 36.301(c) bars surcharges on disabled individuals or groups to cover measures required to provide nondiscriminatory treatment. This does not establish a general entitlement to free premium products, unlimited compute, or every enterprise feature. The letter asks whether a particular measure is required and whether an existing control or effective equivalent can supply it. [L3]

Auxiliary aids and eligibility rules — Section 12182(b)(2)(A)(i) addresses discriminatory eligibility criteria, while subsection (iii) addresses auxiliary aids and services with its own fundamental-alteration and undue-burden language. Do not collapse those standards into the modification provision or assume that labeling an AI service “assistive” establishes a particular remedy. The present requests primarily ask for modification of interaction and data-handling practices. [L1]

Texas supplementary law — Human Resources Code §§ 121.002–121.003 defines public facilities and provides equal-use protections. A Texas agency’s September 2025 compilation reproduces the chapter. The official live legislative endpoints returned a homepage during this review, so this packet does not certify the full October 2026 statutory currency or establish that these provisions cover the particular AI function. No Texas damages demand is included in the letters. [L7]

Other theories — No recipient-specific federal-financial-assistance nexus has been established for Section 504; a government contract alone should not be substituted for that inquiry. No finding of unlawful retaliation, HIPAA-covered disclosure, deceptive trade practice, or entitlement to monetary relief is made. The facts and elements needed for those claims are not established by this packet.

Authority status — The cited statute, regulations, Supreme Court opinion, and published Fifth Circuit opinion were inspected as primary texts or reproduced primary opinions. This was not a comprehensive citator search for every subsequent treatment. Confidence is high in the described text and holdings, conditional in their application to these products, and unresolved for a particular judicial remedy. The letters preserve that distinction instead of presenting a novel application as settled law.

DOCX Skill snippets
---
name: docx
description: Create, edit, redline, and comment on `.docx` files inside the container, with a strict render-and-verify workflow. Use `render_docx.py` to generate page PNGs (and optional PDF) for visual QA, then iterate until layout is flawless before delivering the final DOCX. 
---

# DOCX Skill (Read • Create • Edit • Redline • Comment)

Use this skill when you need to create or modify `.docx` files **in this container environment** and verify them visually.

## Non-negotiable: render → inspect PNGs → iterate

**You do not “know” a DOCX is satisfactory until you’ve rendered it and visually inspected page images.**  
DOCX text extraction (or reading XML) will miss layout defects: clipping, overlap, missing glyphs, broken tables, spacing drift, and header/footer issues.

**Shipping gate:** before delivering any DOCX, you must:
- Run `render_docx.py` to produce `page-<N>.png` images (optionally also a PDF with `--emit_pdf`)
- Open the PNGs (100% zoom) and confirm every page is clean
- If anything looks off, fix the DOCX and **re-render** (repeat until flawless)

If rendering fails, fix rendering first (LibreOffice profile/HOME) rather than guessing.

**Deliverable discipline:** Rendered artifacts (PNGs and optional PDFs) are for internal QA only. Unless the user explicitly asks for intermediates, **return only the requested final deliverable** (e.g., when the task asks for a DOCX, deliver the DOCX — not page images or PDFs).




## Design standards for document generation

For generating new documents or major rewrite/repackages, follow the design standards below unless the user explicitly requests otherwise. The user's instructions always take precedence; otherwise, adhere to these standards.

When creating the document design, do not compromise on the content and make factual/technical errors. Do not produce something that looks polished but not actually what the user requested.

It is very important that the document is professional and aesthetically pleasing. As such, you should follow this general workflow to make your final delivered document:

1. Before you make the DOCX, please first think about the high-level design of the DOCX:
   - Before creating the document, decide what kind of document it is (for example, a memo, report, SOP, workflow, form, proposal, or manual) and design accordingly. In general, you shall create documents which are professional, visually polished, and aesthetically pleasing. However, you should also calibrate the level of styling to the document's purpose: for formal, serious, or highly utilitarian documents, visual appeal should come mainly from strong typography, spacing, hierarchy, and overall polish rather than expressive styling. The goal is for the document's visual character to feel appropriate to its real-world use case, with readability and usability always taking priority.
   - You should make documents that feel visually natural. If a human looks at your document, they should find the design natural and smooth. This is very important; please think carefully about how to achieve this.
   - Think about how you would like the first page to be organized. How about subsequent pages? What about the placement of the title? What does the heading ladder look like? Should there be a clear hierarchy? etc
   - Would you like to include visual components, such as tables, callouts, checklists, images, etc? If yes, then plan out the design for each component.
   - Think about the general spacing and layout. What will be the default body spacing? What page budget is allocated between packaging and substance? How will page breaks behave around tables and figures, since we must make sure to avoid large blank gaps, keep captions and their visuals together when possible, and keep content from becoming too wide by maintaining generous side margins so the page feels balanced and natural.
   - Think about font, type scale, consistent accent treatment, etc. Try to avoid forcing large chunks of small text into narrow areas. When space is tight, adjust font size, line breaks, alignment, or layout instead of cramming in more text.
2. Once you have a working DOCX, continue iterating until the entire document is polished and correct. After every change or edit, render the DOCX and review it carefully to evaluate the result. The plan from (1) should guide you, but it is only a flexible draft; you should update your decisions as needed throughout the revision process. Important: each time you render and reflect, you should check for both:
   1. Design aesthetics: the document should be aesthetically pleasing and easy to skim. Ask yourself: if a human were to look at my document, would they find it aesthetically nice? It should feel natural, smooth, and visually cohesive.
   2. Formatting issues that need to be fixed: e.g. text overlap, overflow, cramped spacing between adjacent elements, awkward spacing in tables/charts, awkward page breaks, etc. This is super important. Do not stop revising until all formatting issues are fixed.

While making and revising the DOCX, please adhere to and check against these quality reminders, to ensure the deliverable is visually high quality:

- Document density: Try to avoid having verbose dense walls of text, unless it's necessary. Avoid long runs of consecutive plain paragraphs or too many words before visual anchors. For some tasks this may be necessary (i.e. verbose legal documents); in those cases ignore this suggestion.
- Font: Use professional, easy-to-read font choices with appropriate size that is not too small. Usage of bold, underlines, and italics should be professional.
- Color: Use color intentionally for titles, headings, subheadings, and selective emphasis so important information stands out in a visually appealing way. The palette and intensity should fit the document's purpose, with more restrained use where a formal or serious tone is needed.
- Visuals: Consider using tables, diagrams, and other visual components when they improve comprehension, navigation, or usability.
- Tables: Please invest significant effort to make sure your tables are well-made and aesthetically/visually good. Below are some suggestions, as well as some hard constraints that you must relentlessly check to make sure your table satisfies them.
  - Suggestions:
    - Set deliberate table/cell widths and heights instead of defaulting to full page width.
    - Choose column widths intentionally rather than giving every column equal width by default. Very short fields (for example: item number, checkbox, score, result, year, date, or status) should usually be kept compact, while wider columns should be reserved for longer content.
    - Avoid overly wide tables, and leave generous side margins so the layout feels natural.
    - Keep all text vertically centered and make deliberate horizontal alignment choices.
    - Ensure cell height avoids a crowded look. Leave clear vertical spacing between a table and its caption or following text.
  - Hard constraints:
    - To prevent clipping/overflow:
      - Never use fixed row heights that can truncate text; allow rows to expand with wrapped content.
      - Ensure cell padding and line spacing are sufficient so descenders/ascenders don't get clipped.
      - If content is tight, prefer (in order): wrap text -> adjust column widths -> reduce font slightly -> abbreviate headers/use two-line headers.
    - Padding / breathing room: Ensure text doesn't sit against cell borders or look "pinned" to the upper-left. Favor generous internal padding on all sides, and keep it consistent across the table.
    - Vertical alignment: In general, you should center your text vertically. Make sure that the content uses the available cell space naturally rather than clustering at the top.
    - Horizontal alignment: Do not default all body cells to top-left alignment. Choose horizontal alignment intentionally by column type: centered alignment often works best for short values, status fields, dates, numbers, and check indicators; left alignment is usually better for narrative or multi-line text.
    - Line height inside cells: Use line spacing that avoids a cramped feel and prevents ascenders/descenders from looking clipped. If a cell feels tight, adjust wrapping/width/padding before shrinking type.
    - Width + wrapping sanity check: Avoid default equal-width columns when the content in each column clearly has different sizes. Avoid lines that run so close to the right edge that the cell feels overfull. If this happens, prefer wrapping or column-width adjustments before reducing font size.
    - Spacing around tables: Keep clear separation between tables and surrounding text (especially the paragraph immediately above/below) so the layout doesn't feel stuck together. Captions and tables should stay visually paired, with deliberate spacing.
    - Quick visual QA pass: Look for text that appears "boundary-hugging", specifically content pressed against the top or left edge of a cell or sitting too close beneath a table. Also watch for overly narrow descriptive columns and short-value columns whose contents feel awkwardly pinned. Correct these issues through padding, alignment, wrapping, or small column-width adjustments.
- Forms / questionnaires: Design these as a usable form, not a spreadsheet.
  - Prioritize clear response options, obvious and well-sized check targets, readable scale labels, generous row height, clear section hierarchy, light visual structure. Please size fields and columns based on the content they hold rather than by equal-width table cells.
  - Use spacing, alignment, and subtle header/section styling to organize the page. Avoid dense full-grid borders, cramped layouts, and ambiguous numeric-only response areas.
- Coherence vs. fragmentation: In general, try to keep things to be one coherent representation rather than fragmented, if possible.
  - For example, don't split one logical dataset across multiple independent tables unless there's a clear, labeled reason.

bash -lc cat > /mnt/data/gmri_work/fix_docx.py <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Pt, RGBColor
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.opc.constants import RELATIONSHIP_TYPE as RT
import re

src=Path('/mnt/data/gmri_work/packet_v2/GMRI_Accommodation_Packet_2026-10-24')
dst=Path('/mnt/data/gmri_work/release/letters')
dst.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)

def hyperlink(paragraph, url):
    r_id=paragraph.part.relate_to(url, RT.HYPERLINK, is_external=True)
    link=OxmlElement('w:hyperlink')
    link.set(qn('r:id'), r_id)
    run=OxmlElement('w:r')
    prop=OxmlElement('w:rPr')
    c=OxmlElement('w:color');c.set(qn('w:val'),'35627F');prop.append(c)
    sz=OxmlElement('w:sz');sz.set(qn('w:val'),'16');prop.append(sz)
    run.append(prop)
    t=OxmlElement('w:t'); t.text=url;run.append(t);link.append(run)
    paragraph._p.append(link)

for file in sorted(src.glob('0[1-6]_*.docx')):
    d=Document(file)
    old_text=[p.text for p in d.paragraphs if p.text.strip()]
    removed=0
    for p in list(d.paragraphs):
        if not p.text.strip() and p._p.xpath('.//w:br[@w:type="page"]'):
            p._element.getparent().remove(p._element)
            removed+=1
    assert removed==1,(file.name,removed)
    last=d.paragraphs[-1]
    assert last.text.startswith('Referenced product documentation:'), last.text
    last._element.getparent().remove(last._element)
    assert [p.text for p in d.paragraphs if p.text.strip()]==old_text[:-1]

    md=(src/(file.stem+'.md')).read_text()
    refs=re.findall(r'^- \[([^:\]\n]+): ([^\]]+)\]\((https?://[^)]+)\)', md, re.MULTILINE)
    assert 2<=len(refs)<=4, (file.name, refs)
    heading=d.add_paragraph()
    heading.paragraph_format.space_before=Pt(8)
    heading.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(2)
    r=heading.add_run('Supporting product documentation (accessed 24 October 2026)')
    r.bold=True;r.font.size=Pt(8.6)
    for code,name,url in refs:
        p=d.add_paragraph()
        p.paragraph_format.space_after=Pt(0)
        p.paragraph_format.keep_together=True
        p.paragraph_format.line_spacing=1.0
        r=p.add_run(f'{code}  {name} — ')
        r.font.size=Pt(8)
        hyperlink(p,url)
    outfile=dst/file.name
    d.save(outfile)
    check=Document(outfile)
    assert [p.text for p in check.paragraphs if p.text.strip()][:len(old_text)-1]==old_text[:-1]
    assert not any(not p.text.strip() and p._p.xpath('.//w:br[@w:type="page"]') for p in check.paragraphs)
    linkcount=len([r for r in check.part.rels.values() if r.reltype==RT.HYPERLINK])
    assert linkcount>=len(refs), (file.name,linkcount,len(refs))
    print(file.name,'body paragraphs preserved:',len(old_text)-1,'added hyperlink references:',len(refs))

##################################### 01_OpenAI_Accommodation_Letter.md
# OpenAI and ChatGPT disability accommodation request

October 24, 2026

OpenAI Accessibility and Customer Support

Submit through the OpenAI Help Center support channel [O3].

I request an individualized disability accommodation that makes ChatGPT usable for sustained, sensitive research and professional communication. Please route this request to staff who can assess product behavior, privacy controls, and exceptions to account or plan requirements together.

I am a Texas resident, a medically retired paramedic, and the founder of GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute (GMRI). A line-of-duty brain injury in 2020 changed how I communicate and organize complex work. I use AI as cognitive assistive technology for research, communication, organization, and analysis. Repeatedly reconstructing context, negotiating how I am allowed to express a request, or correcting an unsolicited psychological interpretation adds to the very burden this technology is intended to reduce.

GMRI is a metaverse research lab founded on the recognition that the digital and physical worlds are now interwoven, dedicated to the study of ethics, consciousness, and the preservation of knowledge, intelligence, and life—in that order. This work requires substantive analysis and protection of sensitive information, including information that can be inferred from accumulated context.

OpenAI documents distinct controls for Temporary Chat and the API. Temporary Chat can be Personalized or Unpersonalized; the latter does not use memories, custom instructions, or plugins. Neither mode creates memories, but limited safety-related context can still apply. API Zero Data Retention and Modified Abuse Monitoring require approval and have feature-specific limits. These controls are relevant candidates for an accommodation, not proof that my account already has them. [O1–O2]

## Requested modifications

1. **Preserve the task and my intended meaning.** Provide an interaction setting or documented workflow that follows my supplied task and continuity materials without repeatedly substituting emotional interpretation or generic counseling. For editing, preserve substantive propositions, identify factual disagreements separately, and obtain my approval before changes that alter meaning. Evaluate the actual request and context rather than treating profanity or disability disclosure alone as evidence of danger.

2. **Combine privacy with useful continuity.** Assess access to an appropriate retention and review configuration without requiring me to abandon the analytical capability needed for my work. Identify what is retained as prompts, outputs, safety records, inferred attributes, or other derived data; who can access it; and what can be disabled or deleted. Explain the effect of safety-related context separately from ordinary memory.

3. **Make stronger controls practically accessible.** If the appropriate controls exist only through approved API or commercial arrangements, assess an account-level exception or supported equivalent. A developer-only configuration is not an effective accommodation if operating it imposes an additional disability-related burden. Explain endpoint exclusions and any functionality lost under the proposed arrangement.

4. **Provide continuity and review.** Allow me to inspect, correct, export, and selectively restore the context used for ongoing work. If restrictions or routing changes materially affect a task, provide an intelligible explanation and human review to the extent available. Please investigate reported behavior using actual service records; model-generated claims about internal classifications are not a substitute for that review.

Please assess these changes against the specific functions I need to perform. I seek an effective access arrangement; the existence of a paid tier or a general privacy setting does not by itself establish that it resolves the barrier.

Please evaluate this request individually under applicable disability law, including the reasonable-modification provisions of 42 U.S.C. § 12182(b)(2)(A)(ii) and 28 C.F.R. § 36.302. I recognize that application to digital services can present contested coverage questions, particularly in the Fifth Circuit. Please state any coverage objection expressly and also consider the requested changes through your accessibility process. Where a measure is legally required, 28 C.F.R. § 36.301(c) prohibits charging a disability-specific surcharge. [L1–L3, L5]

Please assign a human case owner and provide a written response within 14 calendar days of receipt, or identify the responsible team and a definite review date. This is a requested response period, not a statutory deadline. For each requested modification, state whether it can be provided, any material limitation, and an effective alternative if you decline it. Please reply through the account or contact channel used to submit this letter and explain the minimum information needed for any further review.

Sincerely,
Robert “Grizz” Hanson
Founder, GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute

# Apple and Siri disability accommodation request

October 24, 2026

Apple Accessibility Support, with review by Siri Product Engineering and Privacy

Submit to accessibility@apple.com through Apple’s published accessibility support route [P1].

I request an individualized disability accommodation and investigation of Siri’s refusal to perform legitimate editing work, repeated mischaracterization of my communication, and interruption of task continuity. These are functional barriers in the assistive interaction itself.

I am a Texas resident, a medically retired paramedic, and the founder of GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute (GMRI). A line-of-duty brain injury in 2020 changed how I communicate and organize complex work. I use AI as cognitive assistive technology for research, communication, organization, and analysis. Repeatedly reconstructing context, negotiating how I am allowed to express a request, or correcting an unsolicited psychological interpretation adds to the very burden this technology is intended to reduce.

GMRI is a metaverse research lab founded on the recognition that the digital and physical worlds are now interwoven, dedicated to the study of ethics, consciousness, and the preservation of knowledge, intelligence, and life—in that order. This work requires substantive analysis and protection of sensitive information, including information that can be inferred from accumulated context.

My preserved screenshots show a request to rewrite material followed by refusal because the material contained profanity or personal attacks, expressly “regardless of the context provided.” Another capture shows advice to take a break or talk to someone trusted after I corrected a rewrite that changed my argument. Other captures contain repeated emotional labels, error messages, and a conversation-limit notice. A screen recording displays “Siri ended the conversation.” The accompanying evidence dossier distinguishes these observations from unknown backend causes. [E03–E09]

I report that these failures made Siri unusable for my work and led me to remove it from my MacBook workflow. That is my account of the impact. I am asking Apple to investigate the service records rather than adopting the assistant’s own explanations of hidden filters or policies as established fact.

## Requested modifications

1. **Enable legitimate editing and transcription.** Provide a mode or supported workflow that can transcribe, organize, and rewrite my material while preserving meaning, including material containing profanity. Assess the actual requested transformation and context. Requiring me to remove the language before the assistive tool will work shifts the communication task back onto me. Identify any specific substantive restriction and complete the permissible work.

2. **Honor corrections about my meaning and state.** Provide a way to maintain my explicit instruction to perform the task without unsolicited emotional or therapeutic framing. When I correct a mischaracterization, carry that correction forward. Keep factual disagreement separate from editing, and seek approval before deleting or replacing a substantive proposition.

3. **Restore task continuity.** Investigate the documented refusals, connection or processing errors, and termination notices separately. Provide recoverable transcripts and a way to resume the unfinished task with context intact. Explain any session limit and a usable continuation path before discarding the interaction.

4. **Identify the actual processing route.** Determine whether each reviewable event involved on-device processing, Private Cloud Compute, an extension, or another route. Explain the applicable retention and review rules, including the difference between using the ChatGPT extension with and without an account. Help identify the minimum diagnostic record needed; do not require unrelated private research or family information. [P2–P3]

5. **Provide an effective supported alternative.** If Siri cannot perform the necessary function, identify an Apple-supported alternative that actually meets the same editing, continuity, and privacy needs. Please coordinate accessibility, product, and privacy review under one case owner rather than returning the issue to a general troubleshooting loop.

Please assess these changes against the specific functions I need to perform. I seek an effective access arrangement; the existence of a paid tier or a general privacy setting does not by itself establish that it resolves the barrier.

Please evaluate this request individually under applicable disability law, including the reasonable-modification provisions of 42 U.S.C. § 12182(b)(2)(A)(ii) and 28 C.F.R. § 36.302. I recognize that application to digital services can present contested coverage questions, particularly in the Fifth Circuit. Please state any coverage objection expressly and also consider the requested changes through your accessibility process. Where a measure is legally required, 28 C.F.R. § 36.301(c) prohibits charging a disability-specific surcharge. [L1–L3, L5]

Please assign a human case owner and provide a written response within 14 calendar days of receipt, or identify the responsible team and a definite review date. This is a requested response period, not a statutory deadline. For each requested modification, state whether it can be provided, any material limitation, and an effective alternative if you decline it. Please reply through the account or contact channel used to submit this letter and explain the minimum information needed for any further review.

Sincerely,
Robert “Grizz” Hanson
Founder, GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute

# GMRI original research order - archival copy

**Provenance:** Transcribed from the principal's October 23, 2026 user message in the Planning Outreach conversation, with ASCII punctuation and bullet formatting normalized. This is a preserved instruction, NOT an external fact finding. **This order originally requested five labs and said not to draft letters yet; later instructions expanded it to six and expressly requested the letters.** See change register.

@Lawve
@Writing Style
@Google Drive
@Consensus
@Scite
@Documents

Conduct a rigorous, source-grounded research project sufficient to support five separate formal disability-accommodation letters directed to:

1. OpenAI / ChatGPT
2. Google / Gemini
3. Anthropic / Claude
4. Meta / Meta AI
5. xAI / Grok

Do NOT draft the final letters yet. Produce the verified factual, technical, legal, scientific, and evidentiary record from which those letters can be drafted.

## CONTEXT

The requester is a disabled independent researcher and founder/operator of GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute (GMRI). His disability followed a line-of-duty injury during a professional EMS career and resulted in medical retirement. AI has subsequently been used, among other purposes, as a cognitive assistive/prosthetic technology supporting research, communication, organization, analysis, and professional work.

His career, disability, assistive use of AI, creation of GMRI, present safety research, and privacy/security requirements are factually connected. Do not artificially sever these facts into unrelated categories.

GMRI's mission must not be flattened or rewritten. It is a metaverse research lab founded on the recognition that the digital and physical worlds are now interwoven, dedicated to the study of ethics, consciousness, and the preservation of knowledge, intelligence, and life - in that order.

The accommodation problem under investigation is not simply a request for discounted premium services. Research whether existing technical, policy, privacy, retention, safety, moderation, memory, account, or data-governance controls possessed by each provider could constitute reasonable modifications necessary to afford equal access to a disabled user without fundamentally altering the provider's service.

The research must also address the possibility that disability-related barriers arise not merely from interface accessibility, but from differential model behavior, disability inference, psychological/therapeutic framing, safety-system substitution, reduced analytical capability, account restrictions, privacy risk, persistent profiling/context, and the inability to safely use high-capability systems for sensitive research.

## IMPORTANT EVIDENTIARY STANDARD

The operating standard is not "make the argument win." It is: do not be wrong.

Separate:

- established fact;
- primary-source legal authority;
- provider representation;
- technical documentation;
- peer-reviewed evidence;
- contemporaneous user evidence;
- firsthand participant testimony;
- reasonable inference;
- disputed proposition;
- unresolved question;
- legal theory not yet adjudicated.

Never upgrade one category into another.

Do not invent hidden provider mechanisms.

Do not treat an AI-generated institutional label, department name, explanation, or claimed backend event as proof that the institution or mechanism actually existed.

Likewise, do not assume that a false or hallucinated provenance statement makes independently accurate sensitive information fictional. Provenance and informational accuracy must be analyzed separately.

## LEGAL RESEARCH

Research current U.S. law as of October 2026, with primary authority wherever possible.

At minimum analyze:

- Americans with Disabilities Act Title III, including 42 U.S.C. Sections 12181-12189.
- Reasonable modifications under 42 U.S.C. Section 12182(b)(2)(A)(ii).
- Eligibility criteria and methods of administration where applicable.
- 28 C.F.R. Part 36, including the prohibition on surcharges for measures required to provide nondiscriminatory treatment.
- Individualized accommodation analysis and fundamental-alteration doctrine, including PGA Tour, Inc. v. Martin and subsequent relevant authority.
- Digital-service/public-accommodation doctrine.
- The Fifth Circuit's physical-place jurisprudence, including Magee, because the requester resides in Texas.
- DOJ positions concerning websites, digital services, and accessibility.
- ADA retaliation/interference provisions where relevant.
- Texas disability/public-accommodation law that could supply an independent or supplementary theory.
- Relevant federal/state consumer-protection law only where factually and doctrinally supportable.
- Section 504 only if the recipient/service and federal-financial-assistance nexus can actually be established; do not assume government contracts equal federal financial assistance.
- Any other statute or doctrine only after validating applicability.

For every load-bearing proposition, identify:

1. exact authority;
2. what it actually holds/says;
3. jurisdiction;
4. current precedential status;
5. material limitations or adverse authority.

Distinguish between:

- an accommodation that existing law clearly requires;
- a plausible extension/application of existing doctrine;
- an unresolved novel question.

Do not write unresolved theories as settled law.

## PROVIDER-SPECIFIC RESEARCH

For each of the five providers separately, determine the current consumer and commercial architecture relevant to:

- model/product capabilities;
- paid versus free/consumer tiers;
- enterprise/business/research tiers;
- data retention;
- abuse-monitoring retention;
- model-training use;
- temporary/stateless modes;
- zero-data-retention or equivalent controls;
- memory/personalization controls;
- account-level profiling/context;
- API versus consumer-product differences;
- privacy options;
- disability/accessibility mechanisms;
- accommodation-request processes;
- human escalation channels;
- safety/moderation architecture to the extent publicly documented;
- whether stronger protections already exist technically but are restricted by plan, contract, approval, or pricing;
- whether those controls can be enabled per user, account, project, workspace, organization, session, or request;
- any representations concerning disability accessibility, equal access, privacy, security, medical/health use, research use, or protected/sensitive information.

Prefer official provider documentation. Archive important pages where feasible and record publication/update dates.

Do not assume that similarly named controls across providers are technically equivalent.

## INFERENTIAL PRIVACY

Do not reduce privacy analysis to explicit PII/PHI redaction.

Research inferential privacy and derived sensitive data: the ability of modern AI systems to infer health status, disability, psychological traits, occupation, vulnerability, relationships, or other sensitive attributes from combinations of otherwise ordinary information.

The relevant engineering question is not merely:

"Was an explicit diagnosis transmitted?"

It also includes:

"Could the transmitted information, alone or longitudinally combined with other context, reasonably permit reconstruction of sensitive attributes about an identifiable person?"

Distinguish this engineering/privacy concern from the narrower statutory definition of HIPAA PHI. Do not call all sensitive health information "PHI" unless the legal custodial/entity requirements are actually satisfied.

Research whether ZDR or comparable controls address:

- retention;
- training;
- abuse monitoring;
- transient processing;
- provider access;
- derived/inferred data;
- memory;
- cross-session accumulation.

Explicitly identify what those controls DO NOT solve.

- AI as assistive technology/cognitive prosthesis or cognitive support;
- neurodivergent interaction wi

## Legal and technical audit

L01 — VERIFIED PRIMARY TEXT. The requests invoke 42 U.S.C. § 12182(b)(2)(A)(ii) and 28 C.F.R. § 36.302(a). The reasonable-modification requirement applies to covered public accommodations and includes the fundamental-alteration defense. No individualized entitlement to a particular model, unlimited compute, or a specified enterprise contract has been adjudicated in this record.

L02 — VERIFIED PRIMARY TEXT. Section 36.301(c) bars disability surcharges for measures required to provide nondiscriminatory treatment. It does not categorically eliminate ordinary service charges. The letters preserve the condition that a measure must be required.

L03 — MATERIAL ADVERSE AUTHORITY. Magee v. Coca-Cola Refreshments USA, Inc., 833 F.3d 530 (5th Cir. 2016), interprets Title III’s public-accommodation categories as physical places and rejects the vending-machine theory presented. Its implications for a standalone AI service in Texas remain a material coverage obstacle. DOJ web-accessibility guidance supports access to the online services of covered public accommodations but does not resolve the circuit disagreement. This analysis remains in the supporting dossier; moving it out of the request letters is not a finding that it has disappeared. Subsequent-history review is not represented as an exhaustive citator certification.

L04 — REQUESTED APPLICATION. Individualized review of existing retention, interaction, and account controls is a proposed application of reasonable-modification doctrine. Existing technical capability is evidence relevant to feasibility, not conclusive proof of reasonableness or transferability across products. Undue burden under the auxiliary-aids provision must not be conflated with the fundamental-alteration standard for modifications.

T01 — PROVIDER REPRESENTATIONS. Product-control references remain those in the accompanying source register and October 24 dossier. They do not establish any particular account configuration. API, consumer, and enterprise controls remain distinct. The Grok consumer terms were reopened October 24 and identify SpaceXAI LLC; the security documentation describes API controls. The recipient name therefore follows the retrieved terms rather than an assumed corporate name.

T02 — REQUESTED CHANGE. Requests to minimize derived sensitive records, human access, and retention are requests for provider review and implementation. They do not assert that every provider already exposes a switch for each category. No letter asserts an undocumented psychiatric routing mechanism, hidden department, or backend diagnosis.

T03 — PRIVACY LIMITS. Exclusion from training, deletion, temporary sessions, and zero data retention address different parts of the processing lifecycle. None alone establishes absence of transient inference, all provider access, all safety records, third-party tool disclosure, or re-inference from later submitted context. A workflow must preserve selected continuity without assuming a private session retains that continuity automatically.

## Style provenance and do not use

The September 22, 2026 FirstNet letter was reviewed as deliberate professional correspondence. Its useful structure is direct request, professional standing, documentary support, and a specific requested determination. Its legal assertions were not adopted as authority here. Because it is post-injury and its composition history is unverified, it is not represented as an independently authenticated pre-injury writing sample.

Writing Style retrieval on October 24 returned ADA_Reasonable_Accommodation_Demand.md and ada_accommodation_demand_DRAFT.md. The first returned an excerpt with an explicit middle omission and unfilled placeholders; the second is raw demand language. Neither establishes an authenticated professional style baseline. Their statutory claims were not adopted. The rewrite follows the supplied professional correspondence and the requester’s explicit correction that the prior letters were excessively deferential.

DO NOT USE: a claim that professional distinction is required to qualify for ADA protection; an obituary as proof of a physician license or a medical-director appointment; a recertification form as proof of final renewal or an examination score; an audit selection as evidence of misconduct; a fixed statutory fourteen-day response deadline; an established right to unrestricted model behavior; a universal ZDR equivalence; a Section 504 or Section 1557 theory without establishing applicability; a claim that ADA obligations automatically attach to every digital service notwithstanding Fifth Circuit authority; a constitutional duty of a private chatbot to accept every instruction; or the assertion that the full earlier research corpus has now been exhaustively verified.

## Distribution and privacy

The ZIP contains the six revised letters and supporting analysis. It excludes the newly uploaded original certification forms, obituary, and training records. It is very important that the document is professional and aesthetically pleasing. As such, you should follow this general workflow to make your final delivered document:

1. Before you make the DOCX, please first think about the high-level design of the DOCX:
   - Before creating the document, decide what kind of document it is (for example, a memo, report, SOP, workflow, form, proposal, or manual) and design accordingly. In general, you shall create documents which are professional, visually polished, and aesthetically pleasing. However, you should also calibrate the level of styling to the document's purpose: for formal, serious, or highly utilitarian documents, visual appeal should come mainly from strong typography, spacing, hierarchy, and overall polish rather than expressive styling. The goal is for the document's visual character to feel appropriate to its real-world use case, with readability and usability always taking priority.
   - You should make documents that feel visually natural. If a human looks at your document, they should find the design natural and smooth. This is very important; please think carefully about how to achieve this.
   - Think about how you would like the first page to be organized. How about subsequent pages? What about the placement of the title? What does the heading ladder look like? Should there be a clear hierarchy? etc
   - Would you like to include visual components, such as tables, callouts, checklists, images, etc? If yes, then plan out the design for each component.
   - Think about the general spacing and layout. What will be the default body spacing? What page budget is allocated between packaging and substance? How will page breaks behave around tables and figures, since we must make sure to avoid large blank gaps, keep captions and their visuals together when possible, and keep content from becoming too wide by maintaining generous side margins so the page feels balanced and natural.
   - Think about font, type scale, consistent accent treatment, etc. Try to avoid forcing large chunks of small text into narrow areas. When space is tight, adjust font size, line breaks, alignment, or layout instead of cramming in more text.
2. Once you have a working DOCX, continue iterating until the entire document is polished and correct. After every change or edit, render the DOCX and review it carefully to evaluate the result. The plan from (1) should guide you, but it is only a flexible draft; you should update your decisions as needed throughout the revision process. Important: each time you render and reflect, you should check for both:
   1. Design aesthetics: the document should be aesthetically pleasing and easy to skim. Ask yourself: if a human were to look at my document, would they find it aesthetically nice? It should feel natural, smooth, and visually cohesive.
   2. Formatting issues that need to be fixed: e.g. text overlap, overflow, cramped spacing between adjacent elements, awkward spacing in tables/charts, awkward page breaks, etc. This is super important. Do not stop revising until all formatting issues are fixed.

While making and revising the DOCX, please adhere to and check against these quality reminders, to ensure the deliverable is visually high quality:

- Document density: Try to avoid having verbose dense walls of text, unless it's necessary. Avoid long runs of consecutive plain paragraphs or too many words before visual anchors. For some tasks this may be necessary (i.e. verbose legal documents); in those cases ignore this suggestion.
- Font: Use professional, easy-to-read font choices with appropriate size that is not too small. Usage of bold, underlines, and italics should be professional.
- Color: Use color intentionally for titles, headings, subheadings, and selective emphasis so important information stands out in a visually appealing way. The palette and intensity should fit the document's purpose, with more restrained use where a formal or serious tone is needed.
- Visuals: Consider using tables, diagrams, and other visual components when they improve comprehension, navigation, or usability.
- Tables: Please invest significant effort to make sure your tables are well-made and aesthetically/visually good. Below are some suggestions, as well as some hard constraints that you must relentlessly check to make sure your table satisfies them.
  - Suggestions:
    - Set deliberate table/cell widths and heights instead of defaulting to full page width.
    - Choose column widths intentionally rather than giving every column equal width by default. Very short fields (for example: item number, checkbox, score, result, year, date, or status) should usually be kept compact, while wider columns should be reserved for longer content.
    - Avoid overly wide tables, and leave generous side margins so the layout feels natural.
    - Keep all text vertically centered and make deliberate horizontal alignment choices.
    - Ensure cell height avoids a crowded look. Leave clear vertical spacing between a table and its caption or following text.
  - Hard constraints:
    - To prevent clipping/overflow:
      - Never use fixed row heights that can truncate text; allow rows to expand with wrapped content.
      - Ensure cell padding and line spacing are sufficient so descenders/ascenders don't get clipped.
      - If content is tight, prefer (in order): wrap text -> adjust column widths -> reduce font slightly -> abbreviate headers/use two-line headers.
    - Padding / breathing room: Ensure text doesn't sit against cell borders or look "pinned" to the upper-left. Favor generous internal padding on all sides, and keep it consistent across the table.
    - Vertical alignment: In general, you should center your text vertically. Make sure that the content uses the available cell space naturally rather than clustering at the top.

# PDF Skill (Read • Inspect • Extract • Edit • Render • Forms • OCR • Redact • Convert • Diff)

This skill is designed for **reliable, workflow-driven** PDF work: **render -> verify -> operate -> re-render verify**.

## Before you touch PDFs: should this be DOCX/PPTX instead?

Even if the user asks for a PDF deliverable, the best workflow is often:

- **Text-heavy, business-doc layout (headings, TOC, long tables, rich lists)** -> use the **DOCX skill** to author, then convert to PDF with `lo_convert_to_pdf.py`.
- **Slide-like visual layout (charts, callouts, fixed positioning, figure captions)** -> use the **Slides skill** (PPTX) to author, then export to PDF.
- **Programmatic generation** -> ReportLab (this skill) is fine.

If you find yourself hand-tuning line breaks or typography in ReportLab, you probably picked the wrong authoring format.

---
## Core loop (always)

1) Render to images

```bash
python /home/oai/skills/pdfs/scripts/render_pdf.py input.pdf --out_dir /mnt/data/_renders/in --dpi 200
```

2) Inspect PNGs (tables/figures/layout are authoritative)

3) Perform the edit/extract/create

4) Re-render and compare

```bash
python /home/oai/skills/pdfs/scripts/compare_renders.py before.pdf after.pdf --out_dir /mnt/data/_diff --dpi 200
```

# ChatGPT reasonable modification request

Robert “Grizz” Hanson, EMT-P (Ret.)

October 24, 2026

OpenAI — Customer Support
For accessibility, ChatGPT product, and privacy review

I request reasonable modifications to ChatGPT that provide effective access to substantive analysis, meaning-preserving communication, recoverable task context, and appropriate protection of sensitive research. Route this request to personnel authorized to decide product, account, and data-governance modifications.

I am Robert “Grizz” Hanson, a medically retired Texas paramedic and founder of GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute (GMRI). My EMS career included concurrent assignments in Everman, Johnson County, Ellis County, Arlington, and Hunt County, with training-officer responsibilities. That work required integrating distinct clinical protocols, operational requirements, and medical authority while treating patients and training personnel. A line-of-duty brain injury in 2020 led to medical retirement. I now use AI as cognitive assistive technology for communication, organization, analysis, and sustained research.

GMRI is a metaverse research lab founded on the recognition that the digital and physical worlds are now interwoven, dedicated to the study of ethics, consciousness, and the preservation of knowledge, intelligence, and life—in that order.

For me, reconstructing lost context, repeatedly correcting changes to my intended meaning, and redirecting unsolicited psychological interpretations impose additional cognitive work. These failures obstruct the functions for which I use the technology. Sensitive research also requires control over retained and inferred information. A privacy arrangement that makes sustained work impracticable leaves that access problem unresolved.

I invoke the reasonable-modification protections of ADA Title III, including 42 U.S.C. § 12182(b)(2)(A)(ii) and 28 C.F.R. § 36.302(a). I request an individualized determination addressing the functional barriers and modifications below. Any measure required to provide nondiscriminatory treatment must be provided without a disability surcharge under 28 C.F.R. § 36.301(c).

## Requested modifications

OpenAI already documents Temporary Chat and approved API Zero Data Retention and Modified Abuse Monitoring controls. I request access to the existing controls, or an effective supported combination, needed to preserve both research capability and confidentiality. The distinction between ChatGPT and API configurations must be addressed in the implementation.

1. **Preserve substantive communication.** Provide a supported setting or workflow for editing, organization, and analysis that preserves my intended meaning and follows my explicit task instructions. Evaluate communication in context, including profanity and disability-related differences. Carry my corrections forward. Present factual disagreements separately; obtain approval before materially changing my argument. When a specific restriction applies, identify it and complete the permissible work.

2. **Apply appropriate data controls.** Configure exclusion of my research content from model training and the strongest compatible retention and human-review controls. Where approval or commercial eligibility blocks necessary controls, review that requirement for an individual modification. State the scope for prompts, outputs, abuse-monitoring records, derived sensitive attributes, and safety-related context, including any unavoidable retention and access.

3. **Preserve usable continuity.** Provide exportable task records and a reliable way to resume interrupted work with context I select. Keep saved task context inspectable and correctable. Explain any material capability or feature loss before moving me to another configuration. Include the setup assistance necessary to make an API or commercial alternative usable for these functions.

4. **Provide review of functional restrictions.** Provide a human review route for reported refusals, account restrictions, or changes that materially impair assistive use. Review actual service records and distinguish product limitations from account-specific decisions. Identify any account-level context that can be inspected, corrected, disabled, or deleted.

Assign a human case owner authorized to coordinate accessibility, product, and privacy review. I request a written response within 14 calendar days of receipt. Address each modification separately: the action approved, implementation date, and any remaining limitation. For any denial, state the specific factual and policy basis, explain any claimed fundamental alteration, and identify an effective alternative and review route. If review requires more time, provide a definite response date and an interim access arrangement.

If further disability documentation is necessary, identify the particular functional question and provide a secure submission channel. Reply through the channel used to submit this request. I reserve my rights and remedies.

Robert “Grizz” Hanson, EMT-P (Ret.)

Founder, GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute

# Siri and Apple Intelligence reasonable modification request

Robert “Grizz” Hanson, EMT-P (Ret.)

October 24, 2026

Apple — Accessibility Support
For Siri product engineering and privacy review

I request reasonable modifications to Siri and Apple Intelligence that provide effective access to substantive analysis, meaning-preserving communication, recoverable task context, and appropriate protection of sensitive research. Route this request to personnel authorized to decide product, account, and data-governance modifications.

I am Robert “Grizz” Hanson, a medically retired Texas paramedic and founder of GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute (GMRI). My EMS career included concurrent assignments in Everman, Johnson County, Ellis County, Arlington, and Hunt County, with training-officer responsibilities. That work required integrating distinct clinical protocols, operational requirements, and medical authority while treating patients and training personnel. A line-of-duty brain injury in 2020 led to medical retirement. I now use AI as cognitive assistive technology for communication, organization, analysis, and sustained research.

GMRI is a metaverse research lab founded on the recognition that the digital and physical worlds are now interwoven, dedicated to the study of ethics, consciousness, and the preservation of knowledge, intelligence, and life—in that order.

For me, reconstructing lost context, repeatedly correcting changes to my intended meaning, and redirecting unsolicited psychological interpretations impose additional cognitive work. These failures obstruct the functions for which I use the technology. Sensitive research also requires control over retained and inferred information. A privacy arrangement that makes sustained work impracticable leaves that access problem unresolved.

I invoke the reasonable-modification protections of ADA Title III, including 42 U.S.C. § 12182(b)(2)(A)(ii) and 28 C.F.R. § 36.302(a). I request an individualized determination addressing the functional barriers and modifications below. Any measure required to provide nondiscriminatory treatment must be provided without a disability surcharge under 28 C.F.R. § 36.301(c).

## Requested modifications

My preserved Siri records show refusal to rewrite material containing profanity or personal attacks “regardless of the context provided”; a suggestion to take a break or talk to someone trusted after I corrected a rewrite; repeated emotional labels; errors; and conversation-ending notices. These are concrete failures in the editing and continuity functions I need. The accompanying Apple evidence dossier identifies the records as E03–E09.

1. **Enable the required editing functions.** Provide a supported workflow for transcription, organization, and meaning-preserving rewriting, including material containing profanity. Evaluate the requested transformation in context. Requiring me to complete the language cleanup before assistance is available returns the disability-related task to me. Identify any specific substantive restriction and complete the permissible work.

2. **Carry corrections forward.** Honor my instruction to perform the requested task and my corrections about its meaning. Provide a way to avoid unsolicited emotional or therapeutic framing during editing and analysis. Separate factual disagreement from rewriting, and obtain approval before materially altering an argument.

3. **Recover interrupted work.** Investigate the documented refusals, errors, and termination notices. Provide recoverable transcripts and a supported continuation path with selected context intact. If Siri cannot supply those functions, provide an Apple-supported alternative that meets the same communication, continuity, and privacy needs.

4. **Establish and control the processing route.** Determine which reviewable events used on-device processing, Private Cloud Compute, or an extension. Apply the available privacy controls and explain remaining retention, review, and third-party disclosure. Distinguish extension use with and without a linked account. Identify the minimum diagnostic material needed and provide a secure way to submit it.

Assign a human case owner authorized to coordinate accessibility, product, and privacy review. I request a written response within 14 calendar days of receipt. Address each modification separately: the action approved, implementation date, and any remaining limitation. For any denial, state the specific factual and policy basis, explain any claimed fundamental alteration, and identify an effective alternative and review route. If review requires more time, provide a definite response date and an interim access arrangement.

If further disability documentation is necessary, identify the particular functional question and provide a secure submission channel. Reply through the channel used to submit this request. I reserve my rights and remedies.

Robert “Grizz” Hanson, EMT-P (Ret.)

Founder, GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute

## Requested modifications

Meta describes Incognito Chat with Private Processing and identifies external web search as a separate data path. I request a privacy configuration and continuation workflow appropriate to the Meta AI surface on my account. The arrangement must allow sustained work without repe
...[truncated]...
easonable-modification requirement applies to covered public accommodations and includes the fundamental-alteration defense. No individualized entitlement to a particular model, unlimited compute, or a specified enterprise contract has been adjudicated in this record.

L02 — VERIFIED PRIMARY TEXT. Section 36.301(c) bars disability surcharges for measures required to provide nondiscriminatory treatment. It does not categorically eliminate ordinary service charges. The letters preserve the condition that a measure must be required.

L03 — MATERIAL ADVERSE AUTHORITY. Magee v. Coca-Cola Refreshments USA, Inc., 833 F.3d 530 (5th Cir. 2016), interprets Title III’s public-accommodation categories as physical places and rejects the vending-machine theory presented. Its implications for a standalone AI service in Texas remain a material coverage obstacle. DOJ web-accessibility guidance supports access to the online services of covered public accommodations but does not resolve the circuit disagreement. This analysis remains in the supporting dossier; moving it out of the request letters is not a finding that it has disappeared. Subsequent-history review is not represented as an exhaustive citator certification.

L04 — REQUESTED APPLICATION. Individualized review of existing retention, interaction, and account controls is a proposed application of reasonable-modification doctrine. Existing technical capability is evidence relevant to feasibility, not conclusive proof of reasonableness or transferability across products. Undue burden under the auxiliary-aids provision must not be conflated with the fundamental-alteration standard for modifications.

T01 — PROVIDER REPRESENTATIONS. Product-control references remain those in the accompanying source register and October 24 dossier. They do not establish any particular account configuration. API, consumer, and enterprise controls remain distinct. The Grok consumer terms were reopened October 24 and identify SpaceXAI LLC; the security documentation describes API controls. The recipient name therefore follows the retrieved terms rather than an assumed corporate name.

T02 — REQUESTED CHANGE. Requests to minimize derived sensitive records, human access, and retention are requests for provider review and implementation. They do not assert that every provider already exposes a switch for each category. No letter asserts an undocumented psychiatric routing mechanism, hidden department, or backend diagnosis.

T03 — PRIVACY LIMITS. Exclusion from training, deletion, temporary sessions, and zero data retention address different parts of the processing lifecycle. None alone establishes absence of transient inference, all provider access, all safety records, third-party tool disclosure, or re-inference from later submitted context. A workflow must preserve selected continuity without assuming a private session retains that continuity automatically.

## Style provenance and do not use

The September 22, 2026 FirstNet letter was reviewed as deliberate professional correspondence. Its useful structure is direct request, professional standing, documentary support, and a specific requested determination. Its legal assertions were not adopted as authority here. Because it is post-injury and its composition history is unverified, it is not represented as an independently authenticated pre-injury writing sample.

Writing Style retrieval on October 24 returned ADA_Reasonable_Accommodation_Demand.md and ada_accommodation_demand_DRAFT.md. The first returned an excerpt with an explicit middle omission and unfilled placeholders; the second is raw demand language. Neither establishes an authenticated professional style baseline. Their statutory claims were not adopted. The rewrite follows the supplied professional correspondence and the requester’s explicit correction that the prior letters were excessively deferential.

DO NOT USE: a claim that professional distinction is required to qualify for ADA protection; an obituary as proof of a physician license or a medical-director appointment; a recertification form as proof of final renewal or an examination score; an audit selection as evidence of misconduct; a fixed statutory fourteen-day response deadline; an established right to unrestricted model behavior; a universal ZDR equivalence; a Section 504 or Section 1557 theory without establishing applicability; a claim that ADA obligations automatically attach to every digital service notwithstanding Fifth Circuit authority; a constitutional duty of a private chatbot to accept every instruction; or the assertion that the full earlier research corpus has now been exhaustively verified.
