bash -lc cat > /mnt/data/package_gmri_notices.py <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import zipfile,hashlib,shutil,fitz,re
root=Path('/mnt/data/GMRI_ADA_Compliance_Opportunity_2026-10-24')
letters=root/'letters'
ids=['01_OpenAI_ChatGPT','02_Google_Gemini','03_Anthropic_Claude','04_Meta_MetaAI','05_xAI_Grok','06_Apple_Siri']
for name in ids:
 src=root/'renders'/name/(name+'.pdf')
 assert src.exists(),str(src)
 shutil.copy2(src,letters/(name+'.pdf'))

readme='''# GMRI | Formal ADA notices and opportunities to comply | 24 October 2026

The six provider-addressed letters give notice of disability-related access barriers and specify the concrete modifications sought. The receiving companies are responsible for their own compliance, technical determination, corrective action, privacy controls, and written response. No joint research, free GMRI labor, broad disclosure of source material, or waiver is offered.

## Package contents

- `letters/01_OpenAI_ChatGPT.*` - Documented repeated meaning-substitution, ignored corrections, loss of continuity, failed document delivery, and roughly 26 hours of reported work; specific remedies.
- `letters/02_Google_Gemini.*` - Task faithfulness, privacy, continuity, inference controls, and provider-owned remedy.
- `letters/03_Anthropic_Claude.*` - Capable analysis with confidential processing and usable continuity.
- `letters/04_Meta_MetaAI.*` - Private Processing/Incognito continuity and downstream search/inference controls.
- `letters/05_xAI_Grok.*` - ZDR and stateful-function compatibility; confidential recoverable workflow.
- `letters/06_Apple_Siri.*` - Recorded Apple-mediated refusal to edit quoted material (evidence E08), recovery and processor trace.

Each letter is supplied in DOCX (editable), PDF (print/send) and Markdown (accessible plain text). The numbered accommodation actions appear on the first page. The six PDF letters combine into a 12-page review copy separately available alongside this archive.

## Legal basis

All six letters invoke 42 U.S.C. § 12182 and 28 C.F.R. §§ 36.301(c), 36.302(a) and 36.303. They give each provider a 14-calendar-day period, measured from actual receipt, to furnish a substantive written response. That period is the sender's requested response period.

## Evidence boundary

Descriptions of interactions are drawn from user-provided records and statements. OpenAI's October 23-24 record and Apple item E08 are the identified incident-specific evidence. The other four letters identify functional needs and provider configuration issues rather than inventing a particular user-level incident. No private evidentiary corpus or medical record is included in this package. A narrowly selected evidentiary submission can follow through a secure route.

## Important

These are draft correspondence for the founder's review and signature. No letter was transmitted. Previous versions are preserved separately. The paired source register is for the sender, not automatically part of outgoing correspondence. PDF files have been rendered from the paired Word documents and inspected.
'''
(root/'README.md').write_text(readme)

sources='''# Reference register (separate from the outgoing letters)

Primary federal authorities consulted:

- ADA Title III, 42 U.S.C. § 12182: https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title42-section12182&num=0&edition=prelim
- DOJ Title III regulations, 28 C.F.R. Part 36: https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/regulations/title-iii-regulations/
- 28 C.F.R. § 36.301(c): disability-related surcharges for measures required to provide nondiscriminatory treatment.
- 28 C.F.R. § 36.302(a): reasonable modifications to policies, practices and procedures.
- 28 C.F.R. § 36.303: auxiliary aids, effective communication.

Provider materials checked or included in earlier GMRI research record:

- OpenAI ChatGPT data controls: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/7730893-data-controls-in-chatgpt
- OpenAI Memory in ChatGPT: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8590148-memory-in-chatgpt
- Google Gemini Apps Privacy Hub: https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961
- Anthropic Covered Models retention: https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/15425996-data-retention-practices-for-covered-models
- Apple ChatGPT Extension & Privacy: https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/data/en/third-party-ai/

Evidence provenance:

- OpenAI letter: retained October 23-24, 2026 conversation and user-reported ~26-hour burden; earlier GMRI Ship of Theseus/Love Note continuity records.
- Apple letter: GMRI E08 Apple-mediated text-transformation refusal and related retained captures; source component trace remains an investigation for the company.
- Other letters: disability-related functional needs and provider-described controls, not unverified assertions of a specific provider-level incident.

This register documents support for the letters; it is not a provider-owned defense analysis and is not itself a signed evidentiary declaration.
'''
(root/'SOURCE_REGISTER.md').write_text(sources)

m=fitz.open();toc=[]; page=1
for i,name in enumerate(ids):
 p=letters/(name+'.pdf'); d=fitz.open(p)
 assert len(d)==2, (name,len(d))
 m.insert_pdf(d)
 toc.append([1,['OpenAI / ChatGPT','Google / Gemini','Anthropic / Claude','Meta / Meta AI','xAI / Grok','Apple / Siri'][i],page])
 page+=len(d)
m.set_toc(toc)
m.set_metadata({'title':'GMRI - Six Formal ADA Notices and Opportunities to Comply - 2026-10-24',
                'author':'Robert B. Hanson / GrizzlyMedicine Research Institute',
                'subject':'Six provider-directed disability accommodation notices, reviewed copy'})
combined=Path('/mnt/data/GMRI_Six_ADA_Compliance_Notices_Review.pdf');m.save(combined,garbage=4,deflate=True)
openai=Path('/mnt/data/GMRI_OpenAI_ADA_Notice.pdf');shutil.copy2(letters/'01_OpenAI_ChatGPT.pdf',openai)

# Package-level assertions.
for name in ids:
    md=(letters/(name+'.md')).read_text(encoding='utf-8')
    doc=fitz.open(letters/(name+'.pdf'))
    pdftext=' '.join(p.get_text() for p in doc)
    assert all(term.lower() not in md.lower() for term in ['Fifth Circuit','Magee v.','in that order','fundamental alteration','request for permission to do research'])
    assert '14 calendar days' in md
    assert '§ 36.301(c)' in md
    assert 'Actions required to correct the barrier' in doc[0].get_text()
    assert 'Sincerely,' in pdftext
    assert 'GMRI' in md and '2026' in md
    if name.startswith('01_'):
        assert '26 hours' in md and 'six accommodation letters' in md
    if name.startswith('06_'):
        assert 'E08' in md
files=list(sorted(letters.glob('*')))+[root/'README.md',root/'SOURCE_REGISTER.md']
assert len(list(letters.glob('*.docx')))==6 and len(list(letters.glob('*.pdf')))==6 and len(list(letters.glob('*.md')))==6
manifest='\n'.join(hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()+'  '+str(p.relative_to(root)) for p in files)+'\n'
(root/'SHA256SUMS.txt').write_text(manifest)

archive=Path('/mnt/data/GMRI_Six_ADA_Compliance_Notices.zip')
with zipfile.ZipFile(archive,'w',compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,compresslevel=7) as z:
    for p in files+[root/'SHA256SUMS.txt']:
        z.write(p,arcname=str(p.relative_to(root)))
with zipfile.ZipFile(archive) as z:
    assert z.testzip() is None
    actual=z.namelist()
    for item in ('README.md','SOURCE_REGISTER.md','SHA256SUMS.txt'):
        assert item in actual
    for name in ids:
        for ext in ('.pdf','.docx','.md'):
            assert f'letters/{name}{ext}' in actual
    for line in (root/'SHA256SUMS.txt').read_text().splitlines():
        hv,name=line.split('  ',1)
        assert hashlib.sha256(z.read(name)).hexdigest()==hv
assert combined.exists() and archive.exists() and openai.exists()
print('ZIP',archive,'bytes',archive.stat().st_size)
print('REVIEW',combined,'bytes',combined.stat().st_size,'pages',len(fitz.open(combined)))
print('OPENAI',openai,'bytes',openai.stat().st_size)
print('DONE: six Word, six PDF, six Markdown, reviewed PDF, indexed and checksummed archive')

Krouse then specified a federal backstop for chip investors. **Friar answered: “Exactly.”** <Cite refs={["turn689972view1","turn647081search7"]}/>

The reason she gave was financial: OpenAI needs access to cutting-edge chips whose useful economic lifespan is uncertain. Government guarantees could lower borrowing costs and allow substantially more debt financing. That transfers some financing risk from private lenders to the public.

[L12]                Editor’s Note:

[L14]                Here is the text of the Americans with Disabilities
[L15]                Act of 1990 (ADA), including changes made by
[L16]                the ADA Amendments Act of 2008. Congress
[L17]                passed the ADA as a “Public Law,” and it
[L18]                originally was in a different format than
[L19]                presented here. To make the law more widely
[L20]                available, the ADA was later reformatted and
[L21]                published in volume 42 (called “title 42”) of the
[L22]                United States Code. One small part of the ADA is
[L23]                found in title 47 of the United States Code. The
[L24]                text below mirrors the law as it is found in the
[L25]                U.S. Code. Because the numbering system is
[L26]                different in the U.S. Code, the headings provide in

[L30]                                                                    Page 1 of 162
:

[L36]                originally enacted.

[L61]                Sec. 12101. Findings and purpose


[L64]     https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/ada/                                         10/7/26, 8 29 AM

[L68] <IMAGE FOR PAGE: 2 / 162>[image_asset_pointer asset][L69] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 3 / 162>[L70]                         (a) Findings

[L72]                         The Congress finds that—

[L74]                                 (1) physical or mental disabilities in no way diminish a
[L75]                                 person’s right to fully participate in all aspects of
[L76]                                 society, yet many people with physical or mental
[L77]                                 disabilities have been precluded from doing so
[L78]                                 because of discrimination; others who have a record
[L79]                                 of a disability or are regarded as having a disability
[L80]                                 also have been subjected to discrimination;

[L82]                                 (2) historically, society has tended to isolate and
[L83]                                 segregate individuals with disabilities, and, despite
[L84]                                 some improvements, such forms of discrimination
[L85]                                 against individuals with disabilities continue to be a
[L86]                                 serious and pervasive social problem;

[L88]                                 (3) discrimination against individuals with disabilities
[L89]                                 persists in such critical areas as employment,
[L90]                                 housing, public accommodations, education,
[L91]                                 transportation, communication, recreation,
[L92]                                 institutionalization, health services, voting, and
[L93]                                 access to public services;

[L95]                                 (4) unlike individuals who have experienced


[L98]     https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/ada/                                                10/7/26, 8 29 AM
[L99]                                                                                             Page 3 of 162
:
[L102] <IMAGE FOR PAGE: 3 / 162>[image_asset_pointer asset][L103] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 4 / 162>[L104]                                 discrimination on the basis of race, color, sex,
[L105]                                 national origin, religion, or age, individuals who have
[L106]                                 experienced discrimination on the basis of disability
[L107]                                 have often had no legal recourse to redress such
[L108]                                 discrimination;

[L110]                                 (5) individuals with disabilities continually encounter
[L111]                                 various forms of discrimination, including outright
[L112]                                 intentional exclusion, the discriminatory effects of
[L113]                                 architectural, transportation, and communication
[L114]                                 barriers, overprotective rules and policies, failure to
[L115]                                 make modifications to existing facilities and
[L116]                                 practices, exclusionary qualification standards and
[L117]                                 criteria, segregation, and relegation to lesser
[L118]                                 services, programs, activities, benefits, jobs, or other
[L119]                                 opportunities;

[L121]                                 (6) census data, national polls, and other studies
[L122]                                 have documented that people with disabilities, as a
[L123]                                 group, occupy an inferior status in our society, and
[L124]                                 are severely disadvantaged socially, vocationally,
[L125]                                 economically, and educationally;

[L127]                                 (7) the Nation’s proper goals regarding individuals
[L128]                                 with disabilities are to assure equality of opportunity,
[L129]                                 full participation, independent living, and economic
[L130]                                 self-sufficiency for such individuals; and


[L133]     https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/ada/                                              10/7/26, 8 29 AM
[L134]                                                                                           Page 4 of 162
:
[L137] <IMAGE FOR PAGE: 4 / 162>[image_asset_pointer asset][L138] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 5 / 162>[L139]                                 (8) the continuing existence of unfair and
[L140]                                 unnecessary discrimination and prejudice denies
[L141]                                 people with disabilities the opportunity to compete
[L142]                                 on an equal basis and to pursue those opportunities
[L143]                                 for which our free society is justifiably famous, and
[L144]                                 costs the United States billions of dollars in
[L145]                                 unnecessary expenses resulting from dependency
[L146]                                 and nonproductivity.

[L148]                         (b) Purpose

[L150]                         It is the purpose of this chapter—

[L152]                                 (1) to provide a clear and comprehensive national
[L153]                                 mandate for the elimination of discrimination against
[L154]                                 individuals with disabilities;

[L156]                                 (2) to provide clear, strong, consistent, enforceable
[L157]                                 standards addressing discrimination against
[L158]                                 individuals with disabilities;

[L160]                                 (3) to ensure that the Federal Government plays a
[L161]                                 central role in enforcing the standards established in
[L162]                                 this chapter on behalf of individuals with disabilities;
                                and

[L165]                                 (4) to invoke the sweep of congressional authority,
[L166]                                 including the power to enforce the fourteenth

[L177]                                 address the major areas of discrimination faced day-
[L178]                                 to-day by people with disabilities.


[L181]                Sec. 12101 note: Findings and Purposes of ADA
[L182]                Amendments Act of 2008, Pub. L. 110-325, §2, Sept. 25,
[L183]                2008, 122 Stat. 3553, provided that:



[L187]                         (a) Findings

[L189]                         Congress finds that—

[L191]                                 (1) in enacting the Americans with Disabilities Act of
[L192]                                 1990 (ADA), Congress intended that the Act “provide
[L193]                                 a clear and comprehensive national mandate for the
[L194]                                 elimination of discrimination against individuals with
[L195]                                 disabilities” and provide broad coverage;

[L197]                                 (2) in enacting the ADA, Congress recognized that
[L198]                                 physical and mental disabilities in no way diminish a
[L199]                                 person’s right to fully participate in all aspects of
[L200]                                 society, but that people with physical or mental
[L201]                                 disabilities are frequently precluded from doing so
[L202]                                 because of prejudice, antiquated attitudes, or the
[L203]                                 failure to remove societal and institutional barriers;




[L208]     https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/ada/                                                10/7/26, 8 29 AM
[L209]                                                                                             Page 6 of 162
:
[L212] <IMAGE FOR PAGE: 6 / 162>[image_asset_pointer asset][L213] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 7 / 162>[L214]                                 (3) while Congress expected that the definition of
[L215]                                 disability under the ADA would be interpreted
[L216]                                 consistently with how courts had applied the
[L217]                                 definition of a handicapped individual under the
[L218]                                 Rehabilitation Act of 1973, that expectation has not
[L219]                                 been fulfilled;

[L221]                                 (4) the holdings of the Supreme Court in Sutton v.
[L222]                                 United Air Lines, Inc., 527 U.S. 471 (1999) and its
[L223]                                 companion cases have narrowed the broad scope of
[L224]                                 protection intended to be afforded by the ADA, thus
[L225]                                 eliminating protection for many individuals whom
[L226]                                 Congress intended to protect;

[L228]                                 (5) the holding of the Supreme Court in Toyota Motor
[L229]                                 Manufacturing, Kentucky, Inc. v. Williams, 534 U.S.
[L230]                                 184 (2002) further narrowed the broad scope of
[L231]                                 protection intended to be afforded by the ADA;

[L233]                                 (6) as a result of these Supreme Court cases, lower
[L234]                                 courts have incorrectly found in individual cases that
[L235]                                 people with a range of substantially limiting
[L236]                                 impairments are not people with disabilities;

[L238]                                 (7) in particular, the Supreme Court, in the case of
[L239]                                 Toyota Motor Manufacturing, Kentucky, Inc. v.
[L240]                                 Williams, 534 U.S. 184 (2002), interpreted the term



[L244]     https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/ada/                                              10/7/26, 8 29 AM
[L245]                                                                                           Page 7 of 162
:
[L248] <IMAGE FOR PAGE: 7 / 162>[image_asset_pointer asset][L249] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 8 / 162>[L250]                                 “substantially limits” to require a greater degree of
[L251]                                 limitation than was intended by Congress; and

[L253]                                 (8) Congress finds that the current Equal
[L254]                                 Employment Opportunity Commission ADA
[L255]                                 regulations defining the term “substantially limits” as
[L256]                                 “significantly restricted” are inconsistent with
[L257]                                 congressional intent, by expressing too high a
[L258]                                 standard.

[L260]                         (b) Purposes

[L262]                         The purposes of this Act are—

[L264]                                 (1) to carry out the ADA’s objectives of providing “a
[L265]                                 clear and comprehensive national mandate for the
[L266]                                 elimination of discrimination” and “clear, strong,
[L267]                                 consistent, enforceable standards addressing
[L268]                                 discrimination” by reinstating a broad scope of
[L269]                                 protection to be available under the ADA;

[L271]                                 (2) to reject the requirement enunciated by the
[L272]                                 Supreme Court in Sutton v. United Air Lines, Inc., 527
[L273]                                 U.S. 471 (1999) and its companion cases that whether
[L274]                                 an impairment substantially limits a major life
[L275]                                 activity is to be determined with reference to the
[L276]                                 ameliorative effects of mitigating measures;




[L281]     https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/ada/                                               10/7/26, 8 29 AM
[L282]                                                                                            Page 8 of 162
:
[L285] <IMAGE FOR PAGE: 8 / 162>[image_asset_pointer asset][L286] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 9 / 162>[L287]                                 (3) to reject the Supreme Court’s reasoning in Sutton
[L288]                                 v. United Air Lines, Inc., 527 U.S. 471 (1999) with
[L289]                                 regard to coverage under the third prong of the
[L290]                                 definition of disability and to reinstate the reasoning
[L291]                                 of the Supreme Court in School Board of Nassau
[L292]                                 County v. Arline, 480 U.S. 273 (1987) which set forth
[L293]                                 a broad view of the third prong of the definition of
[L294]                                 handicap under the Rehabilitation Act of 1973;

[L296]                                 (4) to reject the standards enunciated by the
[L297]                                 Supreme Court in Toyota Motor Manufacturing,
[L298]                                 Kentucky, Inc. v. Williams, 534 U.S. 184 (2002), that
[L299]                                 the terms “substantially” and “major” in the definition
[L300]                                 of disability under the ADA “need to be interpreted
[L301]                                 strictly to create a demanding standard for
[L302]                                 qualifying as disabled,” and that to be substantially
[L303]                                 limited in performing a major life activity under the
[L304]                                 ADA “an individual must have an impairment that
[L305]                                 prevents or severely restricts the individual from
[L306]                                 doing activities that are of central importance to
[L307]                                 most people’s daily lives”;

[L309]                                 (5) to convey congressional intent that the standard
[L310]                                 created by the Supreme Court in the case of Toyota
[L311]                                 Motor Manufacturing, Kentucky, Inc. v. Williams, 534
[L312]                                 U.S. 184 (2002) for “substantially limits”, and applied



[L316]     https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/ada/                                               10/7/26, 8 29 AM
[L317]                                                                                            Page 9 of 162
:
[L320] <IMAGE FOR PAGE: 9 / 162>[image_asset_pointer asset][L321] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 10 / 162>[L322]                                 by lower courts in numerous decisions, has created
[L323]                                 an inappropriately high level of limitation necessary
[L324]                                 to obtain coverage under the ADA, to convey that it is
[L325]                                 the intent of Congress that the primary object of
[L326]                                 attention in cases brought under the ADA should be
[L327]                                 whether entities covered under the ADA have
[L328]                                 complied with their obligations, and to convey that
[L329]                                 the question of whether an individual’s impairment is
[L330]                                 a disability under the ADA should not demand
[L331]                                 extensive analysis; and

[L333]                                 (6) to express Congress’ expectation that the Equal
[L334]                                 Employment Opportunity Commission will revise that
[L335]                                 portion of its current regulations that defines the
[L336]                                 term “substantially limits” as “significantly
[L337]                                 restricted” to be consistent with this Act, including
[L338]                                 the amendments made by this Act.



[L342]                Sec. 12102. Definition of disability


[L345]                         As used in this chapter:

[L347]                                 (1) Disability

[L349]                                 The term “disability” means, with respect to an



[L353]     https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/ada/                                               10/7/26, 8 29 AM
[L354]                                                                                           Page 10 of 162
:
[L357] <IMAGE FOR PAGE: 10 / 162>[image_asset_pointer asset][L358] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 11 / 162>[L359]                                 individual—

[L361]                                         (A) a physical or mental impairment that
[L362]                                         substantially limits one or more major life
[L363]                                         activities of such individual;

[L365]                                         (B) a record of such an impairment; or

[L367]                                         (C) being regarded as having such an impairment
[L368]                                         (as described in paragraph (3)).

[L370]                                 (2) Major Life Activities

[L372]                                         (A) In general

[L374]                                         For purposes of paragraph (1), major life
[L375]                                         activities include, but are not limited to, caring
[L376]                                         for oneself, performing manual tasks, seeing,
[L377]                                         hearing, eating, sleeping, walking, standing,
[L378]                                         lifting, bending, speaking, breathing, learning,
[L379]                                         reading, concentrating, thinking, communicating,
[L380]                                         and working.

[L382]                                         (B) Major bodily functions

[L384]                                         For purposes of paragraph (1), a major life
[L385]                                         activity also includes the operation of a major
[L386]                                         bodily function, including but not limited to,
[L387]                                         functions of the immune system, normal cell


[L390]     https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/ada/                                                    10/7/26, 8 29 AM
[L391]                                                                                                Page 11 of 162
:
[L394] <IMAGE FOR PAGE: 11 / 162>[image_asset_pointer asset][L395] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 12 / 162>[L396]                                         growth, digestive, bowel, bladder, neurological,
[L397]                                         brain, respiratory, circulatory, endocrine, and
[L398]                                         reproductive functions.

[L400]                                 (3) Regarded as having such an impairment

[L402]                                         For purposes of paragraph (1)(C):

[L404]                                         (A) An individual meets the requirement of
[L405]                                         “being regarded as having such an impairment”
[L406]                                         if the individual establishes that he or she has
[L407]                                         been subjected to an action prohibited under
[L408]                                         this chapter because of an actual or perceived
[L409]                                         physical or mental impairment whether or not
[L410]                                         the impairment limits or is perceived to limit a
[L411]                                         major life activity.

[L413]                                         (B) Paragraph (1)(C) shall not apply to
[L414]                                         impairments that are transitory and minor. A
[L415]                                         transitory impairment is an impairment with an
[L416]                                         actual or expected duration of 6 months or less.

[L418]                                 (4) Rules of construction regarding the definition of
[L419]                                 disability

[L421]                                 The definition of “disability” in paragraph (1) shall be
[L422]                                 construed in accordance with the following:




[L427]     https://www.ada.gov/law-and-regs/ada/                                                  10/7/26, 8 29 AM
[L428]                                                                                              Page 12 of 162
:
[L431] <IMAGE FOR PAGE: 12 / 162>[image_asset_pointer asset][L432] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 13 / 162>[L433]                                         (A) The definition of disability in this chapter
[L434]                                         shall be construed in favor of broad coverage of
[L435]                                         individuals under this chapter, to the maximum
[L436]                                         extent permitted by the terms of this chapter.

[L438]                                         (B) The term “substantially limits” shall be
[L439]                                         interpreted consistently with the findings and
[L440]                                         purposes of the ADA Amendments Act of 2008.

[L442]                                         (C) An impairment that substantially limits one
[L443]                                         major life activity need not limit other major life
[L444]                                         activities in order to be considered a disability.

[L446]                                         (D) An impairment that is episodic or in remission
[L447]                                         is a disability if it would substantially limit a
[L448]                                         major life activity when active.

                                        (E)

[L452]                                               (i) The determination of whether an
[L453]                                               impairment substantially limits a major life
[L454]                                               activity shall be made without regard to the
[L455]                                               ameliorative effects of mitigating measures
[L456]                                               such as—

[L458]                                                   (I) medication, medical supplies,
[L459]                                                   equipment, or appliances, low-vision
[L460]                                                   devices (which do not include ordinary

[L473]                                                 other implantable hearing devices,
[L474]                                                 mobility devices, or oxygen therapy
[L475]                                                 equipment and supplies;

[L477]                                                 (II) use of assistive technology;

[L479]                                                 (III) reasonable accommodations or
[L480]                                                 auxiliary aids or services; or

[L482]                                                 (IV) learned behavioral or adaptive
[L483]                                                 neurological modifications.

[L485]                                             (ii) The ameliorative effects of the mitigating
[L486]                                             measures of ordinary eyeglasses or contact
[L487]                                             lenses shall be considered in determining
[L488]                                             whether an impairment substantially limits a
[L489]                                             major life activity.

[L491]                                             (iii) As used in this subparagraph—

[L493]                                                 (I) the term “ordinary eyeglasses or

The ADA Amendments Act of 2008 expressly states that the primary focus should be **whether covered entities have complied with their obligations**, and that determining whether someone's impairment qualifies as a disability should not require extensive analysis. <FileCite ref="turn60file0" line_range_start={321} line_range_end={331}/>

- **42 U.S.C. § 12102, pages 11–14:** The statute expressly includes reading, concentrating, thinking, communicating, and working among major life activities. - **42 U.S.C. § 12182, pages 96–102:** Title III addresses equal access to covered goods and services, discriminatory administrative practices, unnecessary eligibility barriers, reasonable modifications, and auxiliary aids.
